rows.title: 먼저 도착한 사람
처방_어휘: sustained harmonic pads in the background
rows.처방_SP: Cinematic orchestral score. The piece opens with a solo cello playing a slow, legato melody in the tenor register, answered by a solo oboe carrying a bare counter-melody. A string section provides sustained harmonic pads in the background, moving in gradual volume swells with divisi violins in the upper register. Muted french horns add low, breathy swells beneath, while a grand piano places single sustained notes and sparse arpeggiated figures in the mid register. Orchestral percussion is restrained: a soft timpani roll and one suspended cymbal swell before the final section. The harmony rests on minor seventh and suspended fourth voicings, resolving late. Male tenor vocals enter in a soft, breathy delivery in the lower register, opening into a clear resonant chest voice as the strings rise. Long hall reverb on the vocal, cello and piano creates a spacious acoustic environment with a long natural decay. 62 BPM, D minor, 4/4 time.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Pop ballad featuring a dramatic orchestral arrangement. The track begins with a solo piano playing a melancholic melody in C major at 72 BPM, joined by a solo cello. A baritone male vocal enters with a breathy, intimate delivery. The arrangement builds with a full string section providing legato pads and counter-melodies. Percussion is minimal until the chorus, where a powerful snare and orchestral percussion accents enter. The vocal transitions from a soft chest voice to a powerful, belted tenor range in the higher register during the climax. Acoustic guitar strumming appears in the second verse. The production features high-fidelity clarity with lush hall reverb on the vocals and strings.

rows.title: 빈 홀에서
rows.처방_라벨: Orchestral film score in 3/4 time at 100 BPM
rows.처방_SP: Orchestral film score in 3/4 time at 100 BPM, in E minor. A chamber orchestra plays a slow waltz across an empty auditorium. Divisi cellos and double basses hold sustained root notes beneath the meter while first violins carry a legato melody with warm, unhurried vibrato. A solo harp arpeggiates upward on the third beat of each bar, and a felted upright piano marks the downbeat with soft, pedal-blurred voicings. Clarinet and french horn enter mid-arrangement with long swelling lines. The harmony leans on major seventh and added ninth colours, luminous and unresolved, drifting rather than cadencing. Timpani rolls arrive quietly under the largest phrases; no drum kit. Male tenor vocals sit close and intimate, breathy in the low register and opening to a clear head voice on high phrases, sung in Korean with gentle rubato. Production is natural and wide: hall reverb with a long decay tail, distant room mics, audible bow noise, ending on a sustained string chord fading to silence.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Pop ballad featuring a baritone male vocal with a wide dynamic range. The arrangement centers on a grand piano playing arpeggiated patterns and block chords, accompanied by a lush orchestral string section including violins, violas, and cellos. A concert flute provides melodic counterpoint in the introduction and transitions. The track features a dramatic crescendo into the chorus where the strings become more rhythmic and staccato. The tempo is 72 BPM in 3/4 time, modulating between C major and E major. The production uses high-fidelity hall reverb to create a cinematic space. The vocal performance transitions from a breathy lower register to powerful, sustained chest-voice notes in the higher register during the climax.

rows.title: 접이의자 여든두 개
rows.처방_라벨: Gypsy jazz quartet featuring solo clarinet, acoustic rhythm guitar, upright bass, and accordion
처방_어휘: solo clarinet, acoustic rhythm guitar, upright bass
rows.처방_SP: Gypsy jazz quartet featuring solo clarinet, acoustic rhythm guitar, upright bass, and accordion, recorded live in an empty hall. The acoustic rhythm guitar drives a la pompe pulse — muted staccato chords on the off-beats, dry and percussive, comping under everything. Woody pizzicato upright bass walks in steady quarter notes while the accordion breathes long legato pads and counter-melodies behind the beat. Solo clarinet leads: warm and low in the verses, bright improvised runs and flourishes over the turnarounds, with light vibrato and melodic slides. Warm female vocals, close-miked and intimate, slightly breathy, phrasing lazily behind the beat. Harmony is minor-key and restless, leaning on sweetly unresolved sevenths that slide a step downward before settling home. Swung feel in 4/4 time at 168 BPM in the key of G minor. Clean acoustic production, natural room reverb with a long empty-hall tail, warm analog tone. Nostalgic, wandering, bittersweet.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Pop Jazz-Pop fusion. The arrangement features a prominent clarinet lead, upright bass, acoustic piano, and a swing-style drum kit with crisp snare hits and ride cymbal patterns. An accordion provides harmonic texture and melodic counterpoint. The male vocals are clear and melodic, transitioning between a smooth baritone and a powerful tenor belt in the chorus. The track features syncopated brass stabs and a walking bassline. The tempo is 125 BPM in 4/4 time, likely in the key of F Major.

rows.title: 접이의자 마지막 줄
처방_어휘: melodic movement in the lower register
rows.처방_SP: Bossa nova jazz quartet recorded in a large empty hall after hours, warm and unhurried at 92 BPM in A minor, 4/4. A nylon-string acoustic guitar leads with soft rounded attack, playing rhythmic accompaniment with bossa nova comping patterns, its voicings built on major seventh chords that hang unresolved in the room. The upright bass carries melodic movement in the lower register, walking gently beneath the guitar rather than marking roots. Brushed drums stay quiet on the snare, dry woody cross-stick clicks marking the off-beats with almost no cymbal wash. Acoustic piano enters sparsely, answering the vocal with single-note lines and lush floating chord colors. Breathy female vocals sing close to the microphone in a restrained, conversational tone, slightly behind the beat, with audible breath and little vibrato. Production is intimate and analog: ribbon-microphone warmth, natural room reverb with long empty-hall decay, soft tape compression. Sparse, with silence between phrases.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Indie, bossa nova, jazz pop. Acoustic guitar, upright bass, piano, shaker, and soft percussion. Female vocals. 105 BPM, 4/4 time signature, Key of G Major. The track features a syncopated bossa nova rhythm on the acoustic guitar with nylon strings. The upright bass plays a steady two-beat pattern. A clean piano provides melodic fills and jazz-influenced chords. The female vocals are breathy and intimate, delivered with a relaxed, conversational phrasing. The percussion consists of a light shaker and subtle rim clicks on the snare.

rows.title: 사 초짜리 메아리
rows.처방_라벨: K-Pop power ballad featuring a male tenor vocal
rows.처방_SP: K-Pop power ballad featuring a male tenor vocal, 72 BPM in B minor, 4/4. Opens nearly bare: close-miked upright piano with the sustain pedal held, arpeggiated figures ringing into a wide hall reverb, room tone audible between phrases. The male tenor vocals enter soft and breathy in the lower register, conversational and rubato. A string section swells at the pre-chorus, cellos legato beneath sustained violins; fretless bass and brushed snare join, still restrained. The first chorus lifts into chest voice over shimmering clean guitar arpeggios, and the chorus vocals are doubled for width. Verse two adds palm-muted guitar and eighth-note hi-hat. The bridge strips back to piano and voice alone, then a half-time tom build. The final chorus arrives with full band, driving drums, crash cymbals, overdriven power chords, soaring strings, and a strained belt with falsetto ad-libs. Outro decays to solo piano and a long reverb tail. Korean lyrics throughout.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Pop power ballad. Features a prominent tenor male vocal with a wide dynamic range, transitioning from breathy chest voice to powerful belted notes and soaring head voice. The arrangement begins with a clean electric guitar playing arpeggiated figures and a grand piano. A string section provides sustained legato pads and melodic counterpoints. The drums enter with a standard pop-rock kit, featuring a heavy snare on beats 2 and 4 and driving eighth-note kick patterns. Distorted electric guitars provide thick power chord textures during the choruses. The track is in the key of E Major with a tempo of 72 BPM in 4/4 time. Production includes high-fidelity vocal processing with noticeable plate reverb and delay on the lead vocal.

rows.title: 먼지가 보이는 각도
rows.처방_라벨: Orchestral cinematic score with a focus on woodwinds and strings
처방_어휘: sustained harmonic pads in the background
rows.처방_SP: Orchestral cinematic score with a focus on woodwinds and strings, 66 BPM in C minor, 4/4. A solo flute opens alone with a slow descending line, joined by clarinet in thirds and a low bassoon counter-melody. The string section provides sustained harmonic pads in the background, divisi violas and cellos moving in slow bow swells with almost no vibrato. A harp places single plucked notes at the end of phrases and a celeste answers an octave above. French horns hold soft, distant chords underneath. No drum kit: only a quiet timpani pulse and one suspended cymbal swell before the last section. The harmony moves between minor ninth and suspended second voicings and never fully resolves. Female alto vocals enter low and breathy in the middle register, restrained and almost spoken, sung in Korean with long pauses between phrases. The production is a spacious acoustic environment with a long natural decay, audible room tone between phrases, ending on woodwinds alone.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Pop ballad with orchestral and cinematic elements. The arrangement features a prominent cello lead, grand piano, and a full string section. A baritone male vocalist delivers a dramatic performance with dynamic shifts from breathy, intimate verses to powerful, belted choruses. The percussion is minimal in the verses, evolving into cinematic orchestral drums and crashing cymbals during the climax. The track is in 4/4 time at 72 BPM, in the key of D major.

rows.title: 마루에 남은 걸음
rows.처방_라벨: Tango with a chamber ensemble arrangement
처방_어휘: melodic movement in the lower register
rows.처방_SP: Tango with a chamber ensemble arrangement, 116 BPM in D minor, 4/4. A bandoneon leads with sharp accented attacks on the first and third beats, opening and closing into long breathy sustains. Violin answers with sliding portamento phrases and biting staccato strokes. The double bass anchors the marcato pulse with sustained root notes under each bar, while the cello takes melodic movement in the lower register, dark and singing beneath the violin. An upright piano hammers percussive block chords on the off-beats and drops chromatic runs into the turnarounds. There is no drum kit; the rhythm is carried by string and piano attacks alone. The harmony leans on minor sixth and diminished passing chords, tense and unresolved. Male baritone vocals sit close and dry, spoken-edged and rhythmic in the verses, opening into full chest voice on the refrain, sung in Korean. Recorded live in an empty hall: natural room reverb, audible bellows noise and floor creak. Dramatic, restrained, aching.
rows.재분석_SP: Tango-infused pop theatrical piece in D minor at 120 BPM. The arrangement features a prominent accordion playing staccato rhythmic patterns and melodic flourishes, accompanied by a nylon-string acoustic guitar providing syncopated rhythmic accompaniment. A clean electric guitar adds melodic counterpoint and occasional distorted leads. The percussion consists of a traditional tango-style kit with sharp snare hits and a steady kick drum. A baritone male vocal delivers a dramatic, narrative performance with dynamic shifts between intimate verses and powerful, belted choruses. The bass guitar follows a rhythmic tango pulse, locking with the kick drum. A violin section provides soaring melodic lines and dramatic staccato accents during the bridge and outro.

rows.title: 사운드체크
처방_어휘: full band enters, drums and bass
rows.처방_SP: K-Pop power ballad, 76 BPM in F sharp minor, 4/4. Begins with a single clean electric guitar arpeggio through a wide plate reverb and a felted piano playing sparse mid-register voicings. Male tenor vocals enter close and breathy in the lower register, conversational, with audible breath between lines. A synth pad rises under the pre-chorus with soft string samples layered beneath. At the first chorus the full band enters, drums and bass, a tight kick and snare with a little room around them and a fretless bass sliding between roots, and the chorus vocals are doubled an octave apart for width with a third harmony line panned wide. Verse two adds palm-muted guitar and sixteenth-note hi-hat. The bridge drops to piano and voice, then a half-time tom build lifts into the final chorus with crash cymbals, overdriven power chords and a strained belt. The outro decays to clean guitar and a long reverb tail. Korean lyrics throughout.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Pop rock ballad featuring a male tenor vocalist. The arrangement centers on a clean electric guitar intro with delay and reverb, transitioning into a full band arrangement. Distorted electric guitars provide thick power chord textures in the choruses. A driving drum kit maintains a steady backbeat with prominent crash cymbals and open hi-hats during high-intensity sections. The bass guitar follows the kick drum with a consistent eighth-note pulse. The song is in the key of E Major at 145 BPM in 4/4 time. The vocal performance ranges from intimate chest voice in the verses to powerful, belted high notes and sustained vibrato in the choruses. A melodic electric guitar solo features wide vibrato and blues-influenced bends.

rows.title: 마지막 큐가 끝나고
rows.처방_라벨: Bossa nova and Latin jazz fusion
rows.처방_SP: Bossa nova and Latin jazz fusion, 104 BPM in F major, 4/4. A nylon-string guitar comps syncopated bossa patterns built on major seventh and thirteenth voicings, warm and rounded, sitting slightly behind the beat. Electric piano answers with soft tremolo chords and short single-note fills. Fretless electric bass plays a light two-feel, sliding between notes. The drums stay brushed and quiet, cross-stick on the rim with shaker and woodblock keeping the pulse and the hi-hat barely opening. A muted trumpet takes the head, breathy and close-miked, then trades with a tenor saxophone solo over the turnaround. Female vocals sing soft and conversational with almost no vibrato, drifting into scat adlibs over the second chorus and the outro vamp, sung in Korean. Production is warm and analog: ribbon microphone tone, tape saturation, natural room reverb from a large empty hall, wide stereo guitar. Relaxed, sunlit, a little wistful.
rows.재분석_SP: K-Pop, City Pop. Female vocals, electric guitar, bass guitar, drums, electric piano, synthesizer. 105 BPM, E Major, 4/4 time. The track features a clean, funky electric guitar playing syncopated 16th-note rhythms and muted scratches. A warm electric piano provides harmonic padding with jazz-influenced chord extensions. The bass guitar follows a melodic, walking pattern with occasional slides and pops. The drums maintain a steady backbeat with crisp hi-hat patterns and occasional open hi-hat accents. A smooth female vocal delivery alternates between a breathy chest voice and light falsetto. A melodic electric guitar solo appears in the bridge, utilizing chromatic passing tones and vibrato. Subtle synthesizer pads and occasional chime-like accents provide atmospheric texture.

rows.title: 다시 문을 열면
rows.처방_라벨: Operatic pop ballad with cinematic orchestral arrangements
rows.처방_SP: Operatic pop ballad with cinematic orchestral arrangements, 72 BPM in C minor, 4/4. Opens on a solo grand piano in a large hall, single sustained chords ringing out with the pedal down and room tone audible between them. A female soprano enters in a soft, classically placed head voice, vibrato narrow and controlled, phrasing with rubato. Cellos and low strings swell under the first verse and a boys' choir hums beneath the pre-chorus. The chorus arrives with full band, driving drums, thunderous toms and cymbal crashes under a full string section and brass, with timpani doubling the downbeats. Verse two pulls back to piano, harp and solo violin. The bridge builds through a modulating string ostinato into a key change, and the last chorus carries a massive choir, layered soprano harmonies and soaring operatic adlibs above the melody. Ends on one orchestral hit and a long empty-hall reverb tail. Korean lyrics throughout, sung with operatic diction.
rows.재분석_SP: Musical theater power ballad. Orchestral arrangement featuring a prominent solo violin, grand piano, and a full string section. A baritone male vocalist performs with operatic technique and wide dynamic range. The track begins with a lyrical violin melody over arpeggiated piano. As the vocals enter, the arrangement builds with sustained string pads and orchestral percussion, including timpani rolls and crash cymbals. The tempo is approximately 70 BPM in 4/4 time. The vocal performance utilizes belting in the higher register and vibrato on sustained notes. The production features high-fidelity orchestral recording with natural hall reverb.
